script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: Saying David prayed before packing a single thing adds a detail the passage does not give.
The comparison about most people texting friends and checking the weather before praying risks shaming the baker.
It presents Saul hunting the men as the reason they are nervous. They do not give that reason.
Restless does not necessarily mean itching to go, so the explanation misdefines the answer.
The opening implies the men are afraid because Saul is hunting them. The passage does not say why they are afraid.
Papa addresses the baker as ma'am and sir rather than baker or friend.
Papa asserts that plenty of other things were lying around, although the passage does not say so.
The passage says Keilah has gates and bars, not that it has only one way in.
It states that Saul is coming to Keilah without preserving the situation David asks about. David leaves, and Saul declines to go forth.
The passage does not say that the LORD's answer is exactly why David asks his next question.
It supplies an unstated reason for David's question: that he wanted to know before it was too late.
Saul declining to go forth does not establish that he stays put. The claim that Keilah is never mentioned again in the story also goes beyond the passage.
The passage does not say Saul has free time.
The claim that nobody saw Jonathan's arrival coming assigns knowledge to everyone without support from the text.
The passage does not say David has nothing but his men and some caves.
The passage does not call Jonathan next in line or say he would happily serve beneath David.
Saying Jonathan means it asserts his inner state, which the passage does not state.
It suggests Saul's knowledge explains why he pursues David. The passage does not give that reason.
The definition incorrectly treats every covenant as a promise between two people made in front of God. The passage also does not say their goodbye was quiet or that they will keep this covenant.
The report that David is hiding does not establish that he is not fighting anyone at that moment.
Saying Saul will do the rest goes beyond his stated plan to go with the Ziphites and search.
The passage says David stays in the Wilderness of Maon, not that he stays at the rock.
